turns.question: i am an employee of a board of park commissioners, how is my pension calculated?
turns.answer:
For an employee of a board of park commissioners, Article 12 provides a fixed-benefit retirement annuity. For withdrawals on or after December 31, 2003, the annuity is based on 2.40% for each year of credited service and your highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service. It cannot exceed 80% of that average salary. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

Your age and service determine whether you meet the retirement conditions: age 50 or over with at least 10 years of service, or age 60 or over with at least 4 years of service. If you retire below age 60, the annuity is reduced 1/4 of 1% for each month or fraction of a month that your age is below 60. That reduction does not apply if you retire at age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133] Service of less than a full year is prorated under the statutory service schedule. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

A figure cannot be put to your pension until the fund corrects your record to Article 12; the salary, service, averages, age, and retirement timing currently administered under Article 11 are not the right basis. The fund would need your age at withdrawal, credited service with the fund, highest average annual salary for the required four-year period, and the months or fractions of a month before age 60. Article 12-130 does not apply because its accumulation-based amount is limited to an employee who entered service before July 1, 1971. [40 ILCS 5/12-130]

The federal and state tax treatment of your pension is outside the Pension Code and belongs with the fund, HR, or the IRS.

Article 12 is the pension article for employees of a board of park commissioners and the retirement board administering that fund. Your record currently places you under a different Article, so your own pension comes under that fund, not Article 12. Article 12 covers employees of a board of park commissioners, including classified-service employees, employees in exempt positions, and employees of the retirement board administering the fund. [40 ILCS 5/12-101] The Code defines an employee generally as someone serving a board of park commissioners, subject to exclusions for positions requiring less than 6 months of service during a calendar year, unless the person is already a fund member. [40 ILCS 5/12-118] The Article also covers the retirement board’s employees and certain employees transferred from a park district to a city under the Exchange of Functions Act, with their fund membership preserved. turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. For a qualifying employee with at least 20 years of service, the formula generally uses your highest average annual salary over 4 consecutive years within your last 10 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

- One formula uses different rates for different portions of your service: 1.67% for the first 10 years, 1.90% for the next 10 years, 2.10% for service over 20 through 30 years, and 2.30% for service over 30 years.
- An eligible employee may elect another formula using 2.40% for each year of service for a withdrawal on or after January 1, 2002. That formula may begin at age 55, or at age 50 with at least 30 years of service, and generally has a 0.25% reduction for each month or fractional month the annuity begins before age 60. The reduction does not apply when the applicable service exceptions are met. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- The Code also provides a formula for employees with at least 10 years of service who withdraw on or after January 1, 1999. It begins no earlier than age 60 and uses 2.40% for each year of service for a withdrawal on or after January 1, 2002, subject to an 80% maximum of final average salary. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- The annuity is paid in equal monthly installments. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The figures needed to work out a dollar amount here would be the retirement date or withdrawal date and the age when you would begin the annuity. This is an estimate — your retirement fund makes the binding determination.
